newsitem.title: UK: Firms save up to 10 pct with Mercury - survey.
newsitem.headline: Firms save up to 10 pct with Mercury - survey.

text.p: Small and medium-sized UK firms can save 6.5-10 percent on long-distance calls if they switch from British Telecommunications to Cable and Wireless' subsidiary Mercury Communications, a survey said on Tuesday.

The survey by consultancy and accounting company KMPG was commissioned by Mercury and analysed the calling pattern of over 15,000 businesses. Savings offered by Mercury were compared with the most appropriate BT package, Mercury said in a statement.
BT brushed off the findings, saying BT, Britain's biggest telecoms group, was correspondingly cheaper on other occasions.
But KPMG said for a long-distance bill of 35-200 stg per month, Mercury's VentureCall package undercut BT's Business Choices 1 deal by between eight and 8.3 percent.
Mercury's UK Link package for businesses spending 200-5,000 stg per month, where less than 40 percent was spent on international calls, offered savings of 6.5-10.2 percent.

And GlobalLink, for a long distance call spend of between 200 stg and 5,000 stg, where more than 40 percent was spent on international calls, undercut BT's Business Choices range by 7-10 percent, according to the survey.

Adrian Chamberlain, managing director of Mercury's Business Enterprise Services division, said that he hoped the survey would help smaller enterprises decide which of a host of telephone companies offered the best prices.
"The report demonstrates, very clearly and simply, that small and medium-sized businesses should consider switching to Mercury," he stated.
But a spokesman for BT said a similar survey commissioned a year ago had proved that in some cases, BT was better value.
"If you had different companies with different calling patterns (calling at different times of the day to different countries) would find BT was cheaper," he said.
Cable and Wireless is the second biggest telecoms company in the UK and the 13th largest international carrier in the world.
